lesson.title: English · Past simple affirmative action verbs

skill.name: Past simple affirmative action verbs
skill.definition: Use regular -ed forms and common irregular forms to say what someone did on a completed trip or other past occasion.
success_criteria: Use the past simple form of regular and common irregular action verbs in affirmative sentences about completed events.
Write a short trip account with clear past simple action verbs for completed activities.

lesson.reason: This is one useful past-tense skill for the learner’s goal of describing simple trips. The lesson gives brief explanations and short examples before supported practice and an independent trip account.
lesson.objective: Describe completed trip activities using affirmative past simple sentences with regular and common irregular action verbs.

sections.title: Talk about a finished trip
sections.markdown:
Use the **past simple** for an action that happened and finished in the past. Time words such as *yesterday*, *last weekend*, and *on Saturday* can make the time clear.

*Last weekend, I visited a small town.*

sections.title: Regular verbs: add -ed
sections.markdown:
Many verbs add **-ed**: *visit → visited*, *walk → walked*. If the verb already ends in **e**, add **-d**: *arrive → arrived*. If it ends in a consonant + **y**, change **y** to **i** and add **-ed**: *carry → carried*.

The past form is the same with *I, you, he, she, we,* and *they*: *I walked; she walked.*

sections.title: Irregular verbs: learn the past form
sections.markdown:
Some common trip verbs do not take **-ed**. Learn their past forms: *go → went*, *see → saw*, *take → took*, *eat → ate*, *buy → bought*, and *come → came*.

Use the past form for a finished action: *We went to the beach and saw a boat.* Do not use the present form *go* for that finished action. English also does not use *goed*: the past form is *went*.

sections.title: Tell a simple sequence
sections.markdown: Use one past form for each finished action: *We arrived in the morning, walked by the river, and ate lunch.* Words such as *then* and *later* help show the order. A short trip account can say where you went and what you did there.

worked_examples.title: A regular past form
worked_examples.markdown: *On Sunday, I visited a small town.* The visit is finished, so *visit* becomes *visited*.

worked_examples.title: Two irregular past forms
worked_examples.markdown: *We went to the lake and saw some birds.* *Went* is the past of *go*; *saw* is the past of *see*. Both actions happened on the trip.

worked_examples.title: A short account
worked_examples.markdown: *Last Saturday, I took a bus to the coast. I walked on the beach and ate lunch there.* The verbs *took*, *walked*, and *ate* tell us what happened. Each verb has its past form.

lesson.recap: For finished trip activities, use the past simple: regular verbs often take **-ed** (*walked*), while common irregular verbs have their own forms (*went, saw, took, ate*). Use a past form for each finished action.

tutor.text:
Your lesson is ready: **English · Past simple affirmative action verbs**.

You’ll learn to say what you did on a trip, using forms such as *visited* and *went*. Open the lesson card for a brief explanation and short examples before the practice. It ends with an independent exercise where you write a short trip account.

transcript.learner: Can you explain this section with another short example?

tutor.text: Use the **past simple** when an action is finished. For example: *Yesterday, I walked to the beach.* The walk happened yesterday and is over, so we say **walked**, not *walk*.

transcript.learner: What is this exercise asking me to do? Please do not assess me yet.

tutor.text: Write a short message to a friend about a trip you took. Say what you did, using **past simple** action verbs because the trip is finished. You can write a few sentences; you don’t need to answer it now.

transcript.learner: Item 1: "Last Saturday, I visited a town and walked to a museum. That afternoon, I explored the square and photographed a bridge. That evening, I tasted local food and returned home."

tutor.text: Great work! Your short trip account uses past simple action verbs clearly throughout.

tutor.text:
Your trip account used past-tense action verbs well. **No review is due**, so the next step is saying what you *didn’t* do on a trip.

Open **English · Past simple negatives with action verbs** for a brief explanation, short examples, and practice.

skill.name: Past simple negatives with action verbs
skill.definition: Use did not or didn't plus the base form of an action verb to say that an action did not happen on a completed past occasion.
success_criteria: Form past simple negatives with did not or didn't plus the base form of an action verb.
Use past simple negatives in a short trip account to make clear which activities did not happen.

transcript.learner: What is the most useful thing to remember from this lesson?

tutor.text: For a finished trip, put **each action verb in the past simple**: *I walked to the museum and ate lunch.* Regular verbs often take **-ed** (*walked*); irregular verbs have their own forms (*eat → ate*).
